title: useQueryData
subtitle: Hook that returns only the data value
description: A lightweight hook that returns only the data value from a query, perfect for simple data consumption without loading states.

rows.name: queryKey
rows.description: Unique identifier for the query. Can be a string, array, or object.

rows.name: options
rows.description: Optional configuration object. If no fetcher is provided, uses a previously registered fetcher.

rows.name: options.fetcher
rows.description: Function that returns a Promise resolving to the data. Optional if fetcher was already registered.

returns.description: The fetched data, undefined while loading or on error

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.description: Simple data consumption without loading states

examples.title: With Default Value
examples.description: Provide a default value for better UX

examples.title: Using Registered Fetcher
examples.description: Using useQueryData with a previously registered fetcher

behavior.title: Data Only
behavior.description: Returns only the data value, no loading or error states

behavior.title: Lightweight
behavior.description: Minimal overhead, perfect for simple data consumption

behavior.title: Automatic Caching
behavior.description: Shares cache with other hooks using the same query key

dos: Use for simple data consumption where you don't need loading states
Provide meaningful default values for better UX
Use with TypeScript for type safety
Combine with useQuery when you need loading/error states
donts: Don't use when you need loading or error states
Don't use for complex data transformations
Don't forget to handle undefined values

callouts.title: When to Use
callouts.content: useQueryData is perfect for simple data consumption where you don't need loading states. Use useQuery when you need full state management.
